title: Node.js
blurb: Event loop, Express, streams, clustering and running Node in production.

quiz.question: Why is a long synchronous CPU task dangerous in a Node.js server?
options: It blocks the single event loop, so every other request waits
quiz.explanation: JavaScript runs on one thread per process; while it's busy, no other callbacks run. Offload CPU work to worker_threads, a separate service, or a queue.

quiz.question: In Express 5, an async route handler that throws…
options: Is forwarded to the error-handling middleware automatically
quiz.explanation: Express 5 forwards rejected promises from handlers and middleware to next(err); Express 4 needed a wrapper or explicit try/catch.

quiz.question: Which runs first after the current operation completes?
quiz.explanation: process.nextTick callbacks run before promise microtasks and before the event loop moves to the next phase; overusing it can starve I/O.

quiz.question: How should a Node service handle SIGTERM from Kubernetes?
options: Stop accepting new connections, finish in-flight requests, close DB pools, then exit
quiz.explanation: Graceful shutdown: server.close(), fail readiness, drain in-flight work within the grace period, close resources, then process.exit. Otherwise deploys drop requests.

quiz.question: What does the libuv thread pool handle by default?
options: File-system operations, DNS lookup (getaddrinfo), crypto and zlib work
quiz.explanation: Network I/O uses the OS's non-blocking APIs (epoll/kqueue/IOCP); fs, dns.lookup, crypto and zlib use the pool (4 threads by default, UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE).

problems.title: Streaming a large file
problems.prompt: An endpoint reads a 2 GB CSV with fs.readFile and sends it, and memory spikes. Fix it.
problems.solution: Stream it: await pipeline(fs.createReadStream(path), res) (from node:stream/promises) — or with a Transform stream for processing. pipeline handles backpressure and closes streams on errors, so memory stays flat.

problems.title: Centralised error handling
problems.prompt: Design error handling for an Express 5 API so clients get consistent JSON errors and internals don't leak.
problems.solution: Throw typed errors (e.g., NotFoundError with status 404) from handlers, then add one final app.use((err, req, res, next) => ...) that logs with a request ID and returns { error: { code, message } } with the right status; return a generic 500 message in production. Validate input at the edge; let programmer errors crash and restart under the process manager.
